brief: Goldman's credit desk argues credit is trading a different market than equities: SPX finished roughly flat and Nasdaq made new highs even as rate vol, European sovereign risk, HY decompression and a stressed Paramount Skydance (PSKY) financing hit credit. Earlier in the year higher yields helped credit via yield-based demand; that link is breaking as total returns turn negative and primary supply tests demand, though cleaner positioning, IG yields above 6% and a lighter Q4 supply calendar (about $330bn versus $546bn in Q3) argue for a more constructive medium-term IG technical if rates stabilize. PSKY's roughly $30bn first-lien passed with weaker execution (2.3x versus 3.9x YTD oversubscription) and its IG tranche finished 17bps wider; its roughly $12.4bn second-lien HY tranche fell about 4 points post-pricing, spilling into broader BB/high-beta credit, while loans (+3% YTD) stayed insulated by their floating-rate structure. French fiscal concerns pushed OAT yields about 62bps higher, with the OAT/Bund gap near European-crisis-era levels transmitting into EUR financials. Positioning is already defensive (L/S net leverage near five-year lows, $68bn of SPX futures sold) even as equity volatility stays contained; the desk frames the standoff as either credit and rates stabilizing toward equities or equities eventually catching down.
